source: Written for quran/y4 lesson 31 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Al-Fajr 89:19-24 with words spaced, and the questions)
intro: Lesson 31. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: وَتَأْكُلُونَ ٱلتُّرَاثَ أَكْلًۭا لَّمًّۭا (١٩) وَتُحِبُّونَ ٱلْمَالَ حُبًّۭا جَمًّۭا (٢٠) كَلَّآ إِذَا دُكَّتِ ٱلْأَرْضُ دَكًّۭا دَكًّۭا (٢١)

وَجَآءَ رَبُّكَ وَٱلْمَلَكُ صَفًّۭا صَفًّۭا (٢٢) وَجِا۟ىٓءَ يَوْمَئِذٍۭ بِجَهَنَّمَ ۚ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ يَتَذَكَّرُ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ وَأَنَّىٰ لَهُ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ (٢٣) يَقُولُ يَٰلَيْتَنِى قَدَّمْتُ لِحَيَاتِى (٢٤)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: And you consume inheritance, devouring [it] altogether,
And you love wealth with immense love.
No! When the earth has been leveled - pounded and crushed -
And your Lord has come and the angels, rank upon rank,
And brought [within view], that Day, is Hell - that Day, man will remember, but what good to him will be the remembrance?
He will say, "Oh, I wish I had sent ahead [some good] for my life."

head: Word
Where
Rule
How to read it
rows: Idgham without ghunnah: tanween into ل; then ghunnah on مّ
Madd muttasil: madd then hamza in one word

keywords.def: turning noon or tanween into meem before ب

questions.q: Chunk and link Al-Fajr 89:19-24 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 89:19-24 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 89:19-24 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Find the two ikhfa' examples in 89:21 to 22.
questions.a: «دَكًّۭا دَكًّۭا» (tanween before د) and «صَفًّۭا صَفًّۭا» (tanween before ص).

questions.q: Why does «يَوْمَئِذٍۭ بِجَهَنَّمَ» have a small meem?
questions.a: Iqlab: the tanween before ب turns into a meem with ghunnah.

questions.q: What will a person wish on that Day (89:24)?
options: That he had sent ahead good for his life
questions.a: A) That he had sent ahead good for his life. 89:24: 'Oh, I wish I had sent ahead [some good] for my life.'

questions.q: Al-Fajr 89:20: «وَتُحِبُّونَ ٱلْمَالَ ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: If you could send one good deed ahead to your future, what would it be?
questions.a: On that Day a person will say 'I wish I had sent ahead for my life' (89:24): good deeds are what we send ahead.
